## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Hetugocchaka* constitutes section 2.1 of the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh treatise of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. As part of the *Dukapaṭṭhāna* (conditional relations of dyads), the text systematically investigates the operation of the twenty-four conditional relations (*paccaya*) across the cluster of dyads related to root conditions (*hetu*) originally set forth in the Abhidhamma matrix (*mātikā*). Although the reference passages in the dossier frequently cite the term *hetugocchaka*, they exclusively treat its exposition in the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi* rather than the conditional mechanics elaborated in this section of the *Paṭṭhāna*.

 DharmaNexus nevertheless identifies extensive internal text reuse across the Pali canon, recording 43,387 shared passages across 209 texts [DharmaNexus]. Due to the highly formulaic and combinatorial structure of the *Paṭṭhāna*, the largest reuse occurs with other dyad and triad sections, most prominently the *Mahantaraduka* (Patthana 2.10; 2,882 matches), the *Piṭṭhiduka* (Patthana 2.13; 2,816 matches), the *Dassanenapahātabbahetukattika* (Patthana 1.10; 2,598 matches), the *Cūḷantaraduka* (Patthana 2.2; 2,151 matches), and the *Kusalattika* (Patthana 1.2; 2,500 matches) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus detects cross-language machine alignments with Northern Abhidharma and Yogācāra texts, including Ghoṣaka's *Abhidharmāmṛta*, Asaṅga's *Abhidharmasamuccaya*, the Tibetan translation of the *Yogācārabhūmi*, and Harivarman's *Satyasiddhiśāstra*, reflecting shared Abhidharmic terminology surrounding *hetu* and mental factors [DharmaNexus].
